subject: science
skillName: Speed and the Energy of Motion

items.prompt: Does a moving object have energy?

steps: A moving object has energy of motion.

items.prompt: Which has more energy of motion: a fast object or a slow object of the same size?

steps: More speed means more energy of motion.

items.prompt: A fast ball knocks over more pins than a slow ball. What does this show?

steps: Doing more when it hits something shows the fast ball has more energy.

items.prompt: A toy car moving fast pushes a block farther than a slow car. Which car had more energy?

steps: Pushing the block farther shows the fast car had more energy.

items.prompt: True or false: a slow marble and a fast marble of the same size have the same energy of motion.

steps: The faster marble has more energy of motion.

items.prompt: If you want a ball to move a target farther, should you roll it faster or slower?

steps: A faster ball carries more energy to move the target.

items.prompt: A faster river can carry bigger rocks. Why?
items.answer: It has more energy of motion

steps: Faster moving water has more energy to move larger rocks.

items.prompt: What is the energy an object has because it is moving called?

steps: The energy of a moving object is its energy of motion.

items.prompt: A student rolls the same ball at two speeds into a cup. The fast roll moves the cup farther. What does this test show?
items.answer: The faster ball has more energy

steps: Moving the cup farther is evidence of more energy in the faster ball.

items.prompt: Two identical swings are pushed, one fast and one slow. Which swing could knock a light object away harder?

steps: The faster swing carries more energy of motion.

items.prompt: Explain how to use a target and a marble to show that speed affects energy.
items.answer: Roll the marble slow and then fast at the target and compare how far the target moves

steps: If the target moves farther when the marble is faster, speed affects energy.

items.prompt: Two wind gusts hit a pinwheel. The faster gust spins it harder. What does this tell you about the gusts' energy?
items.answer: The faster gust has more energy

steps: Spinning the pinwheel harder shows the faster gust carries more energy.

items.prompt: Why can a fast-moving car do more damage in a crash than a slow one?
items.answer: A faster car has more energy of motion to transfer

steps: More speed means more energy, which causes more damage on impact.

items.prompt: Describe the evidence you would look for to decide which of two rolling balls has more energy.
items.answer: See which ball pushes or knocks a target farther or harder when it hits

steps: The ball that moves the target more has transferred more energy.

items.prompt: A student claims heavier always means more energy, ignoring speed. Using two identical balls at different speeds, explain why speed also matters.
items.answer: With the same ball, the faster one has more energy, so speed matters too

steps: Because the balls are identical in size, the difference in energy comes from their different speeds.
